description: AI Agents (inside one system): Use when the customer wants something to keep happening by itself inside one system on AI Agent (not for a one-off change: use propose_changes), such as "when a deal is won and the amount is above 5,000, add a kick-off task for the owner and a note". It turns that into one fixed rule on one record type: when (trigger), only if (conditions), then (actions). Before calling it, describe the rule in plain words (when, only if, then, and whether it also acts on records that already match) and get a yes. Nothing runs yet: the answer gives the rule as one sentence, how many records it would have acted on in the last 30 days with examples, and an approval link. Share that link: the rule only starts once the customer approves it there, and from then on the platform runs it again and again without asking. Use describe_record_type for the field keys; each action is one of the actions of propose_changes (set_fields, add_note, add_task and so on), with the values that action takes there. Pass replaces with an automation id to change an existing rule. A rule only acts inside that one system: to sync records between two systems, use an integration (plan_integration). It never deletes and never records a payment.

actions.description: Then: 1 to 3 actions, run in this order on the record that met the rule.

arguments.description: For the other kinds: one item of propose_changes with that action, for the record that met the rule. Use {record.id} as its id and leave type out for the rule's own record type. To act on the contact of an opportunity or other record, give type contact with {record.contact} as its id. A date may be {today} or {today+3} (three days after the rule acts).

clear.description: For set_fields: field keys to empty.

kind.description: The action the rule applies by itself, one of the actions of propose_changes: set_fields to set or empty fields of the record, or update_fields, move_stage, add_note, add_task, update_task, log_activity, add_line_item, link_records or unlink_records.

set.description: For set_fields: field keys and their new values. A date may be {today} or {today+3} (three days after the rule acts).

apply_to_existing.description: Also act once on the records that already match when the rule is switched on. Off by default: the rule then only acts on what happens from now on.

conditions.description: Only if: at most 5 conditions on the same record, all of which must hold. Leave it out when the rule always acts.

field.description: The field key, as describe_record_type names it.

value.description: The value to compare with; not for empty and not_empty, and a number for above and below.

values.description: For one_of: the values the field may hold.

name.description: A short name for the rule, as the customer would call it.

replaces.description: Optional: the id of an earlier automation of the same system that this rule replaces once it is approved.

system.description: Which AI agent: the system's id from get_ai_agents_info, or the name of the system or its connection. Ask the person which AI agent they mean unless they named it in this conversation; never pick one yourself.

trigger.description: When the rule acts: created (a record of the type is made), becomes (a field gets a value, such as a deal becoming won), or changes (a field changes in any way).

field.description: The field key, as describe_record_type names it. Needed for becomes and changes.

value.description: For becomes: the value the field must get, as the system stores it. Leave it out for any value.

type.description: The record type, as get_ai_agents_info lists it: contact, opportunity, invoice, estimate, job, appointment.

name: propose_automation
title: Propose an automation
